messages.message: Export the foreground and background and/or secondary spectra together into the same file.
Enter the sample number you'de like displayed here. You may enter a range of sample numbers similar to '33-39' or '33 to 39', or CSV sample numbers like '34,39,84'

All selected samples and/or detectors will be summed together into a single spectrum.
Caution: if you have both foreground and background selected, they will be summed together.
There are either multiple sample numbers, or multiple detectors that comprise the displayed foreground; checking this option will sum all these to a single spectrum in the output file.
There are either multiple sample numbers, or multiple detectors that comprise the displayed background; checking this option will sum all these to a single spectrum in the output file.
There are either multiple sample numbers, or multiple detectors that comprise the displayed secondary spectrum; checking this option will sum all these to a single spectrum in the output file.
The output spectrum will be the foreground, minus the background.

For each sample number, sum all detectors for that sample number together.
E.g., if you have 8 detectors in your spectrum file, each with 120 samples then the results will have 120 spectra, each of which is the sum of the 8 detectors of the respective samples.

For each detector, sums all sample numbers together.
E.g., if you have 8 detectors in your spectrum file, each with 120 samples then the results will have 8 spectra, each of which is the sum of the 120 samples of their respective detectors.
Removes detector response, peaks, and other analysis results you may have added in InterSpec.
Removes the GPS coordinates from the output file.
A single spectrum will be produced.
Will be summed to single spec.
The currently displayed spectra will be exported, as displayed.

When checked, the spectral data will not lose any information, but for high channel count or high statistics spectra, multiple QR codes may be needed. When unchecked, a wavelet-based lossy compression is used, which loses some information but allows using a QR code with fewer elements, more error correction, or representing any spectrum in a single QR code.
Cannot fit spectrum at this QR size/tolerance
Failed to display spectrum as a QR code: {1}
Failed to refit peak continuums for background-subtracted spectrum; original peak parameters used.

Write the channel counts into the file. Un-check to produce a nuclide-library / calibration-only CAM file, of the same kind GENIE's Library Editor makes. The energy calibration is always written along with a spectrum, so it only becomes a separate option when this is un-checked.
Write the fitted peaks (energy, centroid, FWHM, area and continuum) into the file's peak block, so GENIE sees the same peaks InterSpec fitted. Only Gaussian peaks are written.
Write a GENIE nuclide library built from the identified peaks in the selected samples, so GENIE can search for the same nuclides.
Merge gamma lines that are too close together for the detector to tell apart into a single yield-weighted line, so the library only distinguishes lines GENIE could actually resolve.
The nuclide's key line - the one line GENIE uses to identify and quantify the nuclide. Exactly one line per nuclide is the key line; checking a different line moves it.
No fit yet - click "Fit from peaks..." to determine the FWHM equation.
Write the detector response function's full-energy-peak efficiency curve, converted to the absolute (per gamma emitted at the source) efficiency GENIE expects.

GENIE efficiency curves are absolute (counts per gamma emitted by the source), so the source-to-detector distance the exported curve should describe is needed. Not used for fixed-geometry detector response functions, which are already absolute.
Write the energy calibration into the file. Only offered when no spectrum is being written - a spectrum always carries its calibration, since channel counts are meaningless without it.
Nothing is selected to write - choose at least one of the spectrum, nuclide library, FWHM or efficiency.
Enter a valid source-to-detector distance for the efficiency curve (e.g. "1 m" or "50 cm").
The FWHM has not been fit from the peaks yet - click "Fit from peaks...", or choose a different FWHM source.
No nuclide library lines to write - the selected samples have no peaks identified to a nuclide.
No peaks are identified to a nuclide in the selected samples, so no nuclide library can be built.
Peak at {1} keV is assigned to reaction '{2}', which GENIE nuclide libraries cannot represent, and will not be included.

Peak at {1} keV is assigned to a {2} fluorescence x-ray, which has no parent nuclide and so no half-life to report; it will not be included in the GENIE library. (Decay x-rays, which do have a parent nuclide, are included.)
Peak at {1} keV is an escape peak, which is not an energy the source actually emits, so it will not be included in the GENIE library.
{1} has completely decayed away at the age used, so no line yields could be computed for it.
{1} efficiency point(s) were left out because the absolute efficiency there is negligible at the given distance.
Could not determine the yield of the {1} line at {2} keV; it will not be included.
The detector response function's efficiency could not be well-represented by GENIE's fitted curve form; writing the efficiency points for GENIE to interpolate between instead.
